### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/connector-imap`, `@objectstack/service-mailbox`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **149** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **14** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/connectors/connector-imap/LICENSE`, `packages/connectors/connector-imap/README.md`, `packages/connectors/connector-imap/package.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **14** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/connectors/connector-imap/LICENSE`, `packages/connectors/connector-imap/README.md`, `packages/connectors/connector-imap/package.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 37 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`
- **100** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4adf27a1c0c7f5f95f0357d6c87988552d607ace` — the merge of head `44aabc8775cc1a16ff81f93d6233f2f74465d7fd` into base `404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4adf27a1c0c7f5f95f0357d6c87988552d607ace && git checkout 4adf27a1c0c7f5f95f0357d6c87988552d607ace
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc 44aabc8775cc1a16ff81f93d6233f2f74465d7fd && git checkout -B drift-repro 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc && git merge --no-ff 44aabc8775cc1a16ff81f93d6233f2f74465d7fd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `27aa15166f5a21ddd5e3e4371aa1b13f6580c6f3`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #22871 (body, all 13 comments), ruling `6116489638` on #22870, triage `6137138392`, stage 1's `6145459294` and `6145843378`, claim `6147217218`, the stage-2 `os-dev-report` `6150880990`, seat answer `6151023438`, amendment `6151040021`; PR #23303 body, its one comment (the docs-drift bot), its 50-file list and the net diff against `main`; the check-runs on the head; the head by its sha in read-only git. The API file list and `git diff 175e8d414..27aa15166` agree: 50 files, +3615 / −75 = 3690. The head is 7 commits over the merge base `175e8d414`: `610e112bd` (the liveness flip alone), `1ddc953ae` (the package), `651a2a1cc` (the sync), `bf2f23134`, `3a8fa0423`, the merge `fffc37464`, and `27aa15166` (the census regenerated on the merged tree).

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Scope against the ruled direction — holds.**
- The connector is protocol and auth only: `imap-wire.ts` (framing, values, astring quoting, modified UTF-7), `imap-session.ts` (connect, greeting, CAPABILITY, PLAIN / LOGIN / XOAUTH2, EXAMINE, UID FETCH, LOGOUT), `account.ts`, `imap-error.ts`. No parsing of mail, no dedupe, no store. Zero runtime dependencies (the manifest declares none).
- Decision 4's shape is real: `MailAccount` is one identity with its own `imap` endpoint; `MailCredentialProvider.credentialFor(account)` is called inside `openImapSession` on every open and never cached (pinned: "resolves the credential on every open", 2 opens, 2 asks). `staticCredentials` is the shared mailbox's implementor; the host's `accountFor` resolver in `MailboxServicePlugin({ imap })` is the composition.
- Stage 1 is fed UNCHANGED. `match-records.ts`, `mail-read-visibility.ts`, the three object files other than `sys_mailbox`, and the rematch path have an empty diff against the merge base. `mail-ingest-service.ts` changes one comment line (+2 / −1). The sync calls `ingest({ mailboxId, raw, receivedAt }, { isSystem: true })` and reads only `outcome`. Q1 A (field-level `mailAssociation`, no resolver), Q4 A (`ingest` system-only; `rematch` system / owner / `manage_mailboxes`), Q5 A (additive re-match) are untouched.
- Q3 C phase 1: `parse-message.ts` now treats `message/global` (RFC 6532 §3.7) beside `message/rfc822` as the forwarded-message part read for its headers under source `attachment`, through the new `FORWARDED_MESSAGE_TYPES` set; nested parts are still not read; `inline` is still written nowhere. The ruling's letter names `message/rfc822` (RFC 2046 §5.2.1); `message/global` is that same forward-as-attachment structure with UTF-8 headers, so this is inside phase 1's structured path, not the heuristic stage. It was carried by stage 1's seat as "read it as an `attachment` source, or pin its refusal" and is declared in the changeset, the README and row 47b's neighbour text. Named below as a flag so the maintainer sees the letter-versus-structure reading.
- Nothing out of scope: no per-user sync (the per-user provider is a type, not code), no CalDAV, no write-back (the session has no STORE / EXPUNGE / APPEND / SELECT path at all), no admin plane (no routes, no screens; `sys_mailbox` stays `apiMethods: get, list`), no inline-forward parsing (#23215 stays `Blocked-by: #22871`).

**(b) Security — the stated guarantees hold; three hardening gaps are named in ③.**
- TLS by default: `security` defaults to `'tls'`; `tls.connect` is called with no `rejectUnauthorized` override (Node's default verifies), `servername` set for a host name and omitted for an IP literal (Node then checks IP SANs). No option to disable verification exists. STARTTLS is not offered, which the README states.
- Plaintext refused except loopback, BEFORE a socket opens: `isLoopback` strips brackets, accepts exactly `localhost`, `::1`, and `isIP() === 4 && startsWith('127.')`. Reviewed for the brief's cases: `::1` and `[::1]` accepted; `127.0.0.0/8` accepted; IPv4-mapped `::ffff:127.0.0.1` refused (safe side); `127.1` shorthand, `0.0.0.0`, `LOCALHOST`, `localhost.` and zone-qualified addresses refused (safe side). The one soft spot is `localhost` by NAME: resolution is the OS resolver's, so a hosts-file or resolver compromise on the machine itself could point it elsewhere. That is a host compromise, not a network exposure; flagged, not failing. Pinned by the "refuses security none to any other host before a socket opens" test, which proves no TCP connection was made.
- Credentials: resolved per open (above); never logged — the connector has no logger; `ImapError.response` carries the server's own line only; the sync logs `err.message` and the skip text, never the credential; the double redacts LOGIN / AUTHENTICATE lines in its `commands` log. Never stored on the row: the four new fields are a folder name, two integers and a timestamp; the plugin test pins "no `secret` or `password` typed field on `sys_mailbox`". No new secret store: `staticCredentials` holds a copy in a closure; the host supplies it (H2 measured all four existing connectors take a static credential the same way).
- Read-only is a protocol fact, not a habit: `examine()` sends `EXAMINE` and the session has no `SELECT`; `listMessages` sends `UID FETCH n:* (UID RFC822.SIZE)`; `fetchMessages` sends `UID FETCH set (UID INTERNALDATE BODY.PEEK[])`. No `STORE`, `EXPUNGE`, `COPY`, `MOVE`, `APPEND` or `CLOSE` exists in the code. A `PREAUTH` greeting skips authentication (safe direction).
- Bounded reads: a response line over `IMAP_MAX_LINE_BYTES` (4 MiB) and a literal over `maxLiteralBytes` (default 64 MiB) are refused BEFORE the octets are read; the literal size is parsed from `\d+` and refused unless `Number.isSafeInteger`, so there is no overflow path; a zero-length literal is handled. `RFC822.SIZE` is honoured: the sync lists sizes first and excludes anything over `maxMessageBytes` from the UID set it fetches (pinned: the big message is never fetched). Injection: `EXAMINE` takes `imapAstring(encodeMailboxName(folder))` — CR, LF and 8-bit are UTF-7-encoded away, then `"` and `\` are escaped inside a quoted string; `LOGIN` takes `imapAstring()` of both arguments — printable 7-bit is quoted with escaping, anything else goes as a synchronizing literal sent only after the server's `+` (pinned with a password carrying CRLF); PLAIN and XOAUTH2 payloads are base64; UID sets are built from integers only. No command is built from unescaped text.
- What is NOT bounded (③): the number of parts per response and of untagged responses per command, and the batch's total bytes; and the session's literal cap is not tied to the sync's `maxMessageBytes`.

**(c) The sync state — correct on every axis asked.**
- Reset: a stored cursor applies only when `imap_folder === folder && imap_uid_validity === status.uidValidity`; otherwise `lastUid` starts at 0 and the folder is read from UID 1; `reset: true` is reported only when a cursor existed. A folder with no UIDVALIDITY is refused by the connector (`protocol`), so a cursor is never taken under an untrusted UID space. Pinned: UIDVALIDITY rebuild (2 duplicates, row count 2, cursor re-stamped) and folder change.
- Advance only after handover: `lastUid = entry.uid` is set after `ingest` resolved (`stored`, `duplicate`, `suppressed`), after a deliberate skip (`too_large`, `unreadable`), or when the UID vanished between list and fetch (expunged; nothing to mirror). `saveCursor` runs in `finally` per batch, so a thrown store error leaves the cursor at the last handed-over UID. Pinned: "stops at a store failure with the cursor below the failed message, and the next run retries it" (cursor 1, rows 1; then 2 more, cursor 3).
- Crash in the middle: the worst case is a process kill between an insert and the batch's cursor write; the next run re-lists from the old cursor and every stored message answers `duplicate` through stage 1's unique key `(mailbox_id, dedupe_key)` scoped `organization`. Nothing is skipped; at most one batch is re-fetched.
- The `unreadable` skip is safe: every `VALIDATION_ERROR` `ingest` can throw is either a caller bug the sync cannot produce (missing `mailboxId`; an invalid `receivedAt` — the sync passes a `Date` or `undefined`) or the per-message parse refusal. A transient engine error is not a `VALIDATION_ERROR` and stops the run instead.
- Concurrency: one process — `running` map returns the in-flight promise for the same mailbox, and `syncAll` is serial over mailboxes, so an overlapping `mailbox:imap-sync` run joins the mailbox in flight and starts only mailboxes the first run has not reached. Two processes — both may fetch; the unique key makes the second insert a `duplicate` (stage 1 catches the duplicate-record error and re-reads the winner); a cursor regression from a slower writer only causes a re-fetch of duplicates, never a skip.
- Organization scoping: `syncAll` walks every `sys_mailbox` row (`fields: id`) under the system context — necessarily, it is the process-wide job; `runMailbox` refuses a row with no `organization_id` (`INTERNAL_ERROR`) and hands `organizationId` to `accountFor`; the message's organization is stamped by stage 1 from the mailbox row. Census row 47c names exactly the two system-only doors (`syncMailbox`, `syncAll`) and what they get and lose.
- Teardown: `MailboxServicePlugin.destroy()` cancels `MAILBOX_SYNC_JOB` through `IJobService.cancel` and calls `sync.close()`, which flags `closed`, closes every open session and makes later runs answer `null`; `destroy()` is the only hook the kernel calls (`check-plugin-teardown-shape` header), and the kernel test pins `jobs.cancelled` contains the job after `kernel.shutdown()`. The sync class's own `close()` is not a `Plugin` method, so it is outside that gate's roster by design.

**(d) The four `sys_mailbox` fields — right surface, declared, translated, live.**
- All four are `required: false`, `readonly: true`, `group: 'Sync'`, with descriptions; the plugin test pins `readonly` on each. `readonly` is enforced by the engine's `stripReadonlyFields` for a non-system caller and bypassed for the system context, which is exactly the contract the sync relies on ("written by the sync only" is therefore an enforced statement for every non-system door; `sys_mailbox` has no REST write door at all).
- Placement: `sys_mailbox`'s own header on `main` said the cursor "is added by the ingest half"; #22870's workload line called it the identity half of one object. A separate state object would add a row per mailbox with a 1:1 join for three scalars and a timestamp; the cursor on the mailbox row is the lighter and the planned shape.
- Liveness: `imap_folder`, `imap_uid_validity`, `imap_last_uid` are read in `runMailbox` and written in `saveCursor`; `imap_synced_at` is written in `saveCursor` and read by no code — it is an operator-facing status column served through the `manage_mailboxes` directory read, so declared-and-delivered, but write-only in code (noted).
- Translations: `en` generated from the object; `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES` hand-translated with their source-hash rows; `check:i18n` and `check:i18n-coverage` reported green.

**(e) The `mailAssociation` liveness flip — true, and the anchor resolves.**
- `field.json`: `planned` to `live`, `verifiedAt` 2026-10-13, `authorWarn` and `authorHint` dropped, evidence `packages/services/service-mailbox/src/ingest/match-records.ts#MailRecordMatcher` — `export class MailRecordMatcher` is at line 103 of that file on the head and is unchanged since `82581819b`, so the row is true on `main` today, as stage 1's seat said. The dotted anchor the dispatch spelled is refused by `check:liveness` (one identifier), and the prose names `match` and `flaggedFieldsOf`; the deviation is right.
- `state-counts/field.md` 94 / 4 to 95 / 3, classified 99 unchanged; the `authorWarnedProperties('field')` pin becomes `['conditionalRequired']` with its comment rewritten in the past tense.
- On `origin/main` at `2808069121` the row is still `planned`, and no PR exists yet for `claude/issue-22871-s2-liveness-flip` (the amendment names it). Once that PR lands, merging `main` makes commit `610e112bd` a no-op here, but this PR's changeset would still carry the `@objectstack/spec: patch` line and its spec bullet — see ③.

**(f) Semver and changesets — see ②.**

**(g) The acceptance tests — each clause pinned against the double, with its control; the double is a fair stand-in.**
- `mailbox-sync-service.test.ts` runs on a real `ObjectQL` over `driver-sql` / better-sqlite3 with the real objects and their unique indexes and an app object whose email field declares `mailAssociation: true`. Clause 1: a forward-as-attachment lands as ONE row, `associated`, `match_addresses` carries the customer's address under source `attachment`, one `sys_mail_association` row `matched_by: ingest`, `received_at` equals the IMAP INTERNALDATE; a second test pins EXAMINE, no SELECT, BODY.PEEK and no `\Seen`. Clause 2: the second run fetches 0 and the row count stays 1; a re-delivered copy under a new UID answers `duplicate`; a UIDVALIDITY rebuild re-reads both as duplicates. Clause 3: an unknown sender pools (`unassociated`, no link); after the contact exists, `rematch` adds one link `matched_by: rematch` and moves the row to `associated`. Clause 4: an `Auto-Submitted: auto-replied` message and a `multipart/report` bounce store no row and the cursor moves past both; the control stores a human reply. The incremental-fetch block pins batch and run bounds, the `too_large` skip with its error text, the `unreadable` skip, and the retry-below-failure cursor. `mailbox-sync-kernel.test.ts` boots a real `ObjectKernel` with `ObjectQLPlugin`, a recording job service and the plugin, and pins the schedule shape, a stored-and-associated message through the job handler, `degraded` when the server is gone, and the cancel on shutdown.
- The dev's 11 ablation legs map one to one onto those pins (A1 to clause 1's store, A2 / A2b / A2c to clause 2's three tests, A3 to clause 3, A4 to clause 4, A5 / A5b to the read-only pins, A6 to the loopback refusal, A7 to the two `message/global` parse tests, A8 to the cursor-save pins). Ablations are a report, not a diff; they are not reproducible from here and are recorded as declared.
- The double (`testing.ts`, 430 lines) speaks over a real TCP socket, shares no code with the client, and exercises: server literals (every body is sent as a `BODY[] {n}` literal), client literals only after a `+` continuation, untagged FLAGS / EXISTS / RECENT / OK-coded responses, capabilities in the greeting or on request, SASL-IR and non-SASL-IR PLAIN, the XOAUTH2 error-continuation flow, LOGINDISABLED, `NONEXISTENT`, expunge, UIDVALIDITY rebuild with renumbering, the `n:*` edge, modified UTF-7 folder names, 8-bit bodies byte for byte, and INTERNALDATE with offsets. Not exercised: a multi-literal response, unsolicited untagged responses between commands, a server `BYE`. One inaccuracy in its self-description is in ③.
- H1: an own double rather than `imapkit` (6 days old, 11 releases in 2 days) or `hoodiecrow-imap` (dormant 10 years, deprecated within hours of 3.x) or `wildduck` (MongoDB and Redis) is proportionate for a 5-command read-only subset; the one-off interop probe the dev reports is outside the tree and counts as unmeasured here. The own client (about 1,000 lines) over `imapflow`'s 8 pinned dependencies is likewise proportionate and consistent with the package's zero-dependency claim.

**(h) The surface beyond the claim — each forced by a named gate, and correct.**
- `system-context.mdx` row 47c (`check:system-context-census`): names both doors and both anchors, which exist.
- `tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `…counts.md` (`check:tenant-audit-census`, `tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`): one new site (`mailbox-sync-service.ts` `update` `MAILBOX_OBJECT`, undecidable object name, elevated context), so 228 to 229, 73 to 74, 123 to 124, 167 to 168, 186 to 187, 64 to 65; the six hand-kept prose figures move consistently with the generated table; the stamp names `fffc37464`, the merged parent of the head, which is the tree the census was measured on.
- `llms.txt` 70 to 71 (`check:llms-txt`: non-private `@objectstack/*` workspace packages) and the lockstep count 71 to 72 in `backward-compatibility.mdx` and `publish-smoke-pack.mjs` (`check-lockstep-package-count.mjs`: the `fixed` group's length) are two predicates that differed by one before and after; both are consistent.
- The new package is in the `fixed` group (`check-changeset-fixed`); root README gains its row under the connectors; the lint pin follows the flip; the four translations follow `check:i18n`.
- The lockfile: 15 added lines, two importer entries only — `packages/connectors/connector-imap` with three devDependencies resolved to the same specifier-and-version strings as the neighbouring importers (the vitest peer suffix is byte-identical to the entry above it, `esbuild@0.28.2` included), and the `link:../../connectors/connector-imap` row under `service-mailbox`. No `packages:` / `snapshots:` entry and no integrity line was typed by hand. The hand rebuild is sound, and the head's `Validate Package Dependencies` and `Scaffold outside the monorepo, install, build` checks, which install from this lockfile, are green.

**(i) LICENSE:** byte-identical to `connector-slack`'s and `connector-rest`'s (`git diff` empty). The manifest's `files` (`dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`) matches the other connectors; npm includes LICENSE regardless.

**(j) CI on the head, read three times during this review:** 42 check-runs; 36 success, 5 skipped, 1 still in progress at the last read (`Test Core (3/6)`; `Test Core (4/6)` and `(5/6)` finished green between reads). The five skips are the opt-in or roster jobs (`Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` matrix shard, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`), the same five stage 1's pre-queue read named as `EXPECTED_SKIPS`. No check has failed. `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` are green on the `Part of` body; after the body switches to `Fixes #22871`, the claim `6147217218` names this branch, so the third stays satisfiable. The seat's landing condition "every check green" is not yet met at this read because one shard is still running; the record is on the head, not on that shard. `check:platform-checklist` is deliberately not in per-PR CI (`lint.yml`, maintainer decision) and runs on `main` by the watchdog at 02:51 UTC; its last run (number 41, `287fd6e5d`, 2026-10-13T03:05Z) was green, and 71 commits landed between that sha and the merge base, 8 of them touching the gate's inputs (`docs/qa/platform-checklist` rows re-pointed twice, `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` changes, the security-catalog retirement), so the dev's "red on `main` at `175e8d414`, 8 findings" is plausible and not contradicted by any measurement I can read; it is unverified here, and the next watchdog run is the measurement of record. This diff touches none of its inputs (no `docs/qa/**`, no `metadata-protocol`, no `service-storage` path in the 50 files).

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/connector-imap: minor` — a new published package, first version `18.0.0-next.0`, equal to every other member of the one `fixed` group in pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json` holds only `mode` and `tag`, so there is no `initialVersions` list to extend). Right: the group takes the highest bump, and a new member must enter at the group's version.
- `@objectstack/service-mailbox: minor` — new exports (`MailboxSyncService`, `MAILBOX_SYNC_JOB`, four `DEFAULT_SYNC_*`, `DEFAULT_MAILBOX_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, 11 types), a new constructor option on `MailboxServicePlugin` (backward compatible: the capability boot still constructs it with no arguments), four new fields on the published `sys_mailbox` object, and `message/global` added to the attachment source. Additive; `minor` is right.
- `@objectstack/spec: patch` — a liveness ledger row and its state count, shipped in spec's `files`; no schema or export change. Right as a level. Duplication risk once the flip lands on its own PR: see ③.
- `Clause-②: yes` on the PR body, the changeset and the claim; no `(widening)` / `(narrowing)` arm is needed and none is written. No `major`, no ADR-0087 disposition owed (nothing removed or renamed). `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-empty-changeset` reported green and the head's `Check Changeset` is green.
- Every changeset sentence was checked against the diff and holds: zero runtime dependencies; TLS default with the certificate verified; plaintext only to loopback, before a socket opens; EXAMINE never SELECT; BODY.PEEK never BODY; UIDVALIDITY refusal; per-open credential resolution; the `ImapError` kinds; the `./testing` entry; the job name and interval; the cursor fields and their reset; the advance rule; `maxMessageBytes` 32 MiB; `degraded` to the job service; `message/global`; the export list (matches `index.ts` exactly); "supersedes the ingest seam entry's no mail source feeds the seam" (true: the stage-1 changeset is unreleased and unedited, and this PR's sentence is the one the compiler should carry); "attachments are still not stored" (true).
- `Fixes #22871` under ruling B: correct. Scope items: connector (this PR); folder cursor and UID state, incremental fetch (this PR); dedupe, threading, suppression, the write, the seam call, the stamp, the pool, re-match (stage 1, `82581819b`); attachment extraction moved to #23307, which exists, open, `Blocked-by: #23306`, which exists, open. Acceptance: all four clauses pinned (g). Decision 5 is a semantic the card states, not a code clause. **Findings of this review, none failing the contract:**
1. **Unbounded accumulation per response and per command against a hostile server.** `ImapResponseReader` bounds each LINE (4 MiB) and each LITERAL (64 MiB) but not the NUMBER of parts one response may carry: a server can send an endless run of short literal-marker lines (`{0}` after `{0}`) and `parts` grows without bound; likewise `InFlight.untagged` holds every untagged response of a command with no cap, so an unlimited stream of `* n FETCH` lines before the tagged OK grows memory, and the socket timeout is an inactivity timeout, so a trickle keeps it alive. An IMAP server is an untrusted peer, as the brief says; a total-bytes-per-response and per-command cap (or a count cap) closes the class. Low severity (the host chose the server), owed as hardening.
2. **The sync's `maxMessageBytes` is not the wire bound.** `runMailbox` opens the session without passing `maxLiteralBytes`, so a server that omits or understates `RFC822.SIZE` is bounded by the session default of 64 MiB, not by the configured 32 MiB; and a message above 64 MiB with no or a false size fails the whole run as `protocol` (not a skip) and would do so on every run — the one path on which "one message cannot stall a mailbox" does not hold. Passing `maxLiteralBytes: maxBytes` (plus a small envelope) to `openImapSession` aligns the two bounds; the stall needs a server that lies or omits the size.
3. **A batch is count-bounded, not byte-bounded.** `fetchMessages(fits)` fetches up to `batchSize` (25) messages in one command and holds them all in memory; 25 messages near 32 MiB is about 800 MiB per batch in the worst case. A byte budget per batch is the usual fix.
4. **`localhost` is accepted by name**, not by resolved address (b). Resolution is the OS resolver's; a spoof needs the host itself compromised. Accepting only IP literals would make the rule mechanical.
5. **The double's self-description overstates its `\Seen` control.** `testing.ts`'s header and the connector README say a body fetched "with `BODY[]` (not `BODY.PEEK[]`) or under `SELECT`" is marked `\Seen`; the code marks only `BODY[]` under `SELECT` (`!readOnly`), which is RFC-faithful (EXAMINE never changes state), so neither single mutation A5 (BODY for PEEK, still under EXAMINE) nor A5b (SELECT, still PEEK) can trip the `\Seen` assertion; both legs go red on the command-string regex pins instead, which is what the ablation count reports. The pins are real; the sentence about the double is not. Two words to fix.
6. **A possible duplicate release sentence.** The seat is landing the liveness flip on its own PR first; after that, commit `610e112bd` merges away but this changeset's `@objectstack/spec: patch` line and the spec bullet remain, and the compiler would carry the flip twice. When the flip PR lands with its own changeset, drop the spec line and bullet here (or keep this one and give the flip PR none).
7. **Listing cost on a large folder.** `listMessages(cursor + 1)` returns every UID above the cursor each run, and only then does `maxMessagesPerRun` (500) cut; a 100,000-message folder is re-listed in full on every run until the cursor catches up. Correct, not cheap; a note for the per-user phase.
